MAJOR: `transitions()` calls `_git("diff", …)` without `allow_fail`, so a missing `develop`/`origin/develop` (common in shallow or feature-branch CI checkouts) now raises RuntimeError where it previously returned empty — this can break the module's documented `--report exits 0` contract unless an unshown entrypoint catches it.

`_load` reads the working tree (`p.read_text`) while diffing `base..HEAD`: uncommitted edits or local deletions flip the count (locally reverted `completed` → undercount; file present in HEAD but deleted in worktree → silently `None`/skipped). Fail-open relative to the AC's fail-closed intent; committed state should be read via `git show HEAD:rel`.

`store-registry.json` gains a root-level wildcard `BI-TEST-*.json` with no explanation and outside the AC scope; depending on the list's semantics it either ingests test artifacts into an item store or excludes genuine `BI-TEST-*` items from tracking — needs justification and anchoring to a directory.
MINOR: `transitions()` emits an extra JSON line on stderr (skip event), violating the module's stated "Output is one JSON line on stderr" contract for strict downstream parsers.
The skip event reports only a count, not the skipped paths; without path-level detail the original "silently skipped" problem is only half solved for operators.
AC states JSONDecodeError propagates, but it is converted to RuntimeError (chained via `from e`); callers or tests matching JSONDecodeError will never observe it.
`_git` has `timeout=20` but does not catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` (only `_repo_root` does); a slow git call produces an uncaught traceback and non-JSON stderr instead of a structured failure.
`git show base:rel` uses `allow_fail=True`: any failure (invalid base, corrupt object) collapses to `prev={}` → status not DONE → item counted as a fresh transition (fail-open on the baseline side).

id-blocks ledger: `reserved_up_to` jumps 1470→1477 with no session recording IDs 1470–1476; verify those were reserved by other machines, otherwise the allocation ledger has an unexplained gap (leak, not collision).
No test covers the new skip event or asserts the printed end-to-end completion count; coverage stops at `_load`/`transitions` units, leaving the AC's "gate prints the real completion count" unproven.
NIT: `import pytest` is added for `pytest.raises` only — confirm the test-framework runner is pytest, since the file previously had zero third-party deps.
`functools.lru_cache` on `_repo_root` is process-global; safe today only because tests monkeypatch the name — a mid-process repo-root change would serve stale data.

`Path.resolve()` follows symlinks, so a legitimate in-repo symlink pointing to a shared items directory outside the top-level now fails closed as "escapes the repo root" — confirm that layout is impossible.
Per the language rule, this is tooling Python / an edit to shipped Python; worth stating explicitly in the PR so it isn't later read as "new shipped logic → Go".
SUMMARY: Direction is right: git-top-level resolution, fail-closed loading, and focused temp-repo tests directly address the AC and remove the old product-forge/ROOT join bug.

Top risks are behavioral regressions around git failures (potential `--report exits 0` break), still evaluating working-tree rather than committed HEAD content, and an unjustified out-of-scope store-registry wildcard.
Before merge: confirm entrypoint exception handling, switch reads to `HEAD:rel`, and justify or drop the `BI-TEST-*.json` registry pattern.
